claim: The movie written by Edward Hume, a 1982 film that aired in 1983, was the seventh highest rated non-sports show and featured a Kansas state highway. The De Soto High School (Kansas) is located off this highway.
evidencia:
Page: K-10 (Kansas highway). Sentence: K-10 is a 38-mile (61 km) state highway in the U.S. state of Kansas.
Page: K-10 (Kansas highway). Sentence: Several scenes for the TV-movie "The Day After" were filmed on the highway in 1982 portraying a mass exodus evacuating the Kansas City area on I-70.
Page: The Day After. Sentence: The Day After is an American television film that first aired on November 20, 1983, on the ABC television network.
Page: The Day After. Sentence: With a 46 rating and a 62% share of the viewing audience during its initial broadcast, it was the seventh highest rated non-sports show up to that time and set a record as the highest-rated television film in history—a record it still held as recently as a 2009 report.
Page: De Soto High School (Kansas). Sentence: The school is located off of K-10 and Lexington Avenue on 91st street.
Page: Edward Hume. Sentence: Edward Hume (born May 18, 1936, in Chicago) is an American film and television writer, best known for creating and developing several TV series in the 1970s, and for writing the 1983 TV movie "The Day After".
